slides.title: Activity Levels Across CPAT, SISEPUEDE, CBAM and FTT
slides.subtitle: Put four climate models on one baseline, and count the carbon price once
slides.message: Linked climate models disagree before any policy is applied. One driver layer over ten activities puts them on one baseline, applies the carbon price's effect on demand exactly once, and checks that cars stay inside travel.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity
slides.notes: Companion to the public CPAT-AI repository. Every claim about the models was checked against their public code on 31 October 2026.

slides.title: Where the models' own values fail against the evidence, the layer replaces them

points.text: SISEPUEDE's example grows regional travel at 2.64 times income growth with no ceiling; the evidence says mobility rises roughly in proportion with income (Schafer and Victor 2000).
its example moves every industrial elasticity to 1 by 2050; steel and cement demand rise for decades, then level off (van Ruijven et al. 2016).
ownership grows about twice as fast as income at low and middle incomes, then saturates (Dargay and Gately 1999).
CPAT's elasticity of 0.8 becomes 0.92 at $3,000 per person and 0.48 above $22,000.

slides.source: Working paper 6.4, Table 2; SISEPUEDE example data; CPAT-AI elasticity table and income factor.

slides.title: Left unchecked, car travel overtakes all travel, even with a saturating ownership curve

points.text: a 30% car share of passenger travel reaches 100% in about 56 years at 2% income growth.
does not prevent it: the crossing still comes in year 54, at 363 vehicles per 1,000.
check every year that cars × km per car × occupancy stay below total travel, and let km per car adjust.

slides.source: Working paper 6.4, Proposition 3 and Appendix A.

slides.title: The data gaps bind as hard as the method

points.text: no car fleet data for 21 of 71 regions (Nigeria, South Africa, Pakistan and Kenya among them); industrial heat ships without data; steel only inside E3ME-FTT.
one public example country; country calibrations are not public.
co-benefits always use the engineering road model's driving, whatever road model is selected (issue I100).
that a rule-based link is second-best to solving models together: none of the four was built for that, and written rules are easier to audit.
